title: Pension — East rural farmers and fishers
insight: Score as highly as existing holders on insurance understanding (76% vs 45%) — consistent with a distribution barrier rather than an awareness one. Understanding is partly a result of already owning a product, so this gap is read as a correlate, not proof.
recommendation: Village Ejo Heza agents + mobile money sign-up, pitched as flexible low contributions. The largest single segment in this analysis — mostly Ubudehe 2, low-income rural households — so closing it directly advances NST2's resilience and poverty-reduction goals, not just inclusion statistics.

title: Pension — Kigali urban salaried
insight: Nearly identical to existing holders on every measure — the clearest quick win in the data.
recommendation: Employer payroll partnerships; RSSB voluntary top-up alongside salaried benefits. This segment is already affluent and formally employed — the case here is administrative ease and fast conversion, not poverty reduction.

title: Insurance — East rural farmers and fishers
insight: Score higher on insurance understanding than existing holders (95% vs 63%); a quarter live over an hour from a branch — consistent with physical access, not information, being the constraint.
recommendation: Bundle crop/livestock micro-insurance with existing cooperative schemes. Low-income, Ubudehe 2 households — a direct line to NST2's rural resilience target: a single bad harvest no longer means catastrophic loss.

title: Pension — North rural farmers and fishers
insight: Smaller gap between holders and lookalikes than other segments — genuinely on the fence rather than mismatched.
recommendation: Same village-agent channel as the East rural segment; standard Ejo Heza tier. Ubudehe 3 households slightly better-off than the East segment, but still a poverty-resilience case, not just an inclusion number.

title: Insurance — Kigali urban salaried
insight: Score higher on insurance understanding than existing holders (92% vs lower) — not an education gap.
recommendation: Bundle life/credit-life insurance with an existing bank or SACCO loan. Affluent, formally employed — a commercial-market opportunity, not a poverty-reduction target.
